pages.title: my / your / his / her + 's
rules: his = for a man; her = for a woman. The word depends on the OWNER, not the thing.
Use 's for possession: Sara's brother = the brother of Sara.
Sara's can also be Sara is: Sara's happy. Check the context.
examples: A mãe da Sara é a Nadia.

pages.head: The photo on the wall
text: On the wall of Sara's living room there is a big family photo. In the middle there are her grandmother and grandfather. They are smiling. Next to them are her mother and father. Her mother's name is Nadia and her father's name is Karim.
In front there are Sara, her brother and her two sisters. "This is my family," says Sara to a visitor. "It's a big family, but we are very close."
Every Sunday the family has lunch together. Grandma cooks and Grandpa tells stories. The children help and the parents talk. Sara loves Sundays.
tf: Sara's grandparents are in the middle of the photo.
The family has lunch together every Sunday.
pages.talk: Who cooks in your family? When does your family eat together?

pages.title: Family: fact file
text: In English, 'mom' (USA) and 'mum' (UK) are the short forms of mother. 'Dad' is short for father.
A family can be 'nuclear' (parents + children) or 'extended' (with grandparents, uncles, cousins).
Family names are important: Smith, Brown, Silva. Parents and children often share a last name.
